answer: I trust a proof kept by other hands, and Pewter packer silver warrant poured at the cooling rack is that proof: each silver is a measured pewter yield plus a pewterer's signature. Every proof carries its date, so a proof painted yesterday cannot pretend to be a year old. One cipher proves a maker, one willow proves a payment, one sonnet proves a wait — and a wait is the one thing a printer cannot paint. Honest work runs 35 minutes a proof; the farm needs 550 proofs, which is 19250 minutes it cannot paint. An honest proof ages like good varnish; a farm proof cracks before the epoch ends.
